carol_cust: Hey team — since we flipped over our service to use Redwood PrivateLink this morning we're seeing intermittent 502s from the API. Happens ~1-3x/min for a handful of requests, latency spikes too. No app changes on our side. Sharing minimal repro and logs below.

carol_cust: curl output (from app VM in customer VPC):
```
$ curl -v https://inference.private.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
* About to connect() to inference.private.redwood.example.com port 443 (#0)
* Connected to inference.private.redwood.example.com (10.1.5.22) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (0)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"BadGateway", "message":"upstream read error"}
```

carol_cust: We also captured a short tcpdump on the VM. Saw a lot of retransmits and RSTs to the endpoint IP. Not sure if this is on our side or the endpoint.

alice_support: Thanks Carol — sorry for the disruption. Can you confirm whether the PrivateLink endpoint is an interface endpoint (ENI) in your VPC? Also any NLB/ALB in front of the service on our side? We'll need a small set of checks:
- tcpdump from your VM during a failure (1-2 minutes)
- output of `openssl s_client -connect <endpoint_ip>:443 -alpn h2 -servername inference.private.redwood.example.com -brief`
- `traceroute -T -p 443 <endpoint_ip>` (TCP traceroute)

ben_infra: FYI, PrivateLink for this service uses an NLB in front of the backend fleet and TLS is terminated at the backend (we do TLS passthrough on the NLB). If the customer's client is doing ALPN h2, the backend needs to speak h2. If we see TLS termination accidentally happening at the NLB (misconfigured listener), it can cause 502s. Also healthcheck behavior: if targets go unhealthy then NLB returns 502 for some flows.

dave-deploy-bot: deployment 2026-02-19T09:12:03Z created: target-group-proxy-v2 updated listeners: tcp:443 -> forwarded unchanged

emma_network: Quick network note — ephemeral port/NACL/Security Group issues are common when you put an interface endpoint inside multiple subnets with restrictive NACLs. NLB health checks and return packets need ephemeral ranges open. Check NACLs on the subnets with the ENIs and on the route tables.

carol_cust: Attaching the tcpdump excerpt (filtered to the endpoint IP) and openssl output we ran. tcpdump shows SYN, SYN-ACK, then large gap, then RST from endpoint.
```
12:03:21.123456 IP 10.0.2.14.51524 > 10.1.5.22.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:03:21.123789 IP 10.1.5.22.443 > 10.0.2.14.51524: Flags [S.], seq 0 ack 1
12:03:21.456000 IP 10.1.5.22.443 > 10.0.2.14.51524: Flags [R], seq 1
12:03:21.456100 IP 10.0.2.14.51524 > 10.1.5.22.443: Flags [R], seq 1
```

carol_cust: openssl output:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.1.5.22:443 -alpn h2 -servername inference.private.redwood.example.com -brief
CONNECTED(00000003)
Protocol : TLSv1.3
Cipher : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
ALPN protocol: h2
---
220 bytes read
write:errno=104
```

alice_support: Thanks — the RSTs and errno=104 (connection reset by peer) strongly point to an intermediate device or the endpoint target resetting. Two immediate suspects: 1) NACL/SG blocking ephemeral ports causing asymmetric replies; 2) NLB target health/ALPN mismatch on backend proxies.

alice_support: Can you run the following from one of your app VMs and paste outputs?
```
# 1) confirm ephemeral port range and test an outbound TCP session to ephemeral port - see what source port is used
python - <<'PY'
import socket, sys
s=socket.socket()
s.connect(("10.1.5.22",443))
print(s.getsockname())
s.close()
PY

# 2) tcpdump with full 3-way handshake and window sizes:
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/pl-debug.pcap host 10.1.5.22 and port 443
```

carol_cust: Ran the python snippet — source port 51820. Also ran tcpdump for 2 mins and uploaded pcap to the support bucket id xxxxx.

ben_infra: We pulled the pcap. Observed many SYN->SYN-ACK->RST like you pasted. On our side the NLB target group shows intermittent Unhealthy -> Healthy flaps around the same timestamps. The NLB health check uses a TCP connect check to 443 on the backend proxy. If the backend occasionally rejects ALPN h2 negotiation the proxy sometimes resets causing the health check flaps.

ben_infra: Can you check your subnet NACLs and the SG attached to the interface endpoint ENI(s)? We need to verify ephemeral return traffic isn't being dropped. Typical ephemeral port range to allow is 32768-60999 (or the VPC default). Also ensure there is no restrictive stateful SG on the ENI that only allows specific source ports.

emma_network: Also confirm there is no route policy doing NAT somewhere that rewrites source ports. If there is a NAT gateway, outbound connections from the app to the endpoint will come from the NAT's elastic IP with different ephemeral ranges. NLB healthcheck expects connectivity back to targets directly.

carol_cust: Found a restrictive NACL on the private subnet used for the interface endpoint: inbound rules only allowed 443 and 80, and outbound allowed established only for 1024-32767 — so our source port 51820 is being blocked on return (51820 > 32767). I think that explains the RSTs.

carol_cust: I updated the NACL to allow ephemeral range 32768-65535 outbound/inbound and kept a short maintenance window. Also confirmed Security Group on ENI allows ephemeral reply ports.

alice_support: Great find. After NACL change, can you run a continuous curl loop and we will monitor NLB target health and logs on our side?

carol_cust: Running loop now: `while true; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://inference.private.redwood.example.com/v1/generate; sleep 1; done`

carol_cust: After the NACL change we still saw a couple of 502s in the next 5 minutes. tcpdump shows successful handshakes but occasional upstream resets still.

ben_infra: That points to a second issue — ALPN/protocol mismatch on the backend proxy. Our backend proxies advertise both h2 and http/1.1 but an older proxy instance in the target group was using an older TLS config that didn't properly negotiate h2 causing an upstream read error. I've kicked a rolling restart for the target group and patched the proxy to support ALPN h2 consistently.

dave-deploy-bot: deployment 2026-02-19T10:07:42Z rolling-restart target-group-proxy-v2 started (3 instances)

carol_cust: After the restart and NACL change we've been running the curl loop for 30 minutes with zero 502s and stable p95 latency. No more retransmits in tcpdump.

alice_support: Excellent. Summary of root causes and remediation: 
- Root cause 1: Customer subnet NACL was blocking ephemeral return ports (source port >32767) causing many TCP sessions to be reset. Remediated by allowing ephemeral range 32768-65535.
- Root cause 2: One older backend proxy instance had TLS/ALPN config that didn't advertise h2 consistently, causing occasional upstream read errors and NLB health flaps. Remediated by rolling restart and ALPN config patch on target group.

alice_support: Preventative recommendations: 
- Ensure NACLs and SGs allow ephemeral port ranges for PrivateLink interface endpoints.
- If using NAT or centralized egress, ensure healthcheck flows from NLB targets align with NAT behavior.
- Monitor NLB target health and ALPN mismatch errors: check proxy logs for `negotiation failed` or `no matching protocol` messages.

carol_cust: Thanks everyone — we'll keep an eye on this and let you know if anything else crops up. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

ben_infra: Glad we got this stable. Filing a runbook note and adding an internal ticket to check other target groups for ALPN drift.

alice_support: Closing the thread in 24h if no regressions. If you see anything, ping this thread and we'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
